designSummary: Difference-in-differences for attendance and cost, combined into an incremental cost-effectiveness ratio with bootstrap uncertainty.
sampleSize: About 1,050 women a year book at the two group-care hubs and about 2,300 at the other four. With attendance near 50 percent, the standard error of the difference-in-differences is about 2.6 percentage points (square root of 0.25/1,050 times 2 plus 0.25/2,300 times 2), so the analysis has 80 percent power at two-sided alpha 0.05 for a difference of about 7.4 points, below the 13-point difference seen in the trial (claim c1). The cost side has no power calculation: costs are estimated with intervals.
primaryAnalysis: Linear probability model for attendance with hub group, period and their interaction, standard errors clustered by hub; the same for cost per woman; the ratio with 2,000 bootstrap replicates resampling women within hubs, shown on a cost-effectiveness plane and an acceptability curve over a range of values the board might place on an additional attender.
secondaryAnalysis: Results for women under 20, women new to the country and women with a previous loss; sensitivity analyses for group size, interpreter costs and excluding the first three months of group care.
missingData: Women who transfer out are kept in the hub of booking up to transfer; missing invoices are reported and costed at the median.
multiplicity: One primary ratio; subgroup and sensitivity results descriptive.
software: R; code and cost inputs archived before analysis.
overfittingGuards: Comparison and outcome fixed before analysis
Subgroups limited to three named groups
summary: About 7.4 points detectable for attendance; the cost-effectiveness ratio reported with bootstrap intervals.
